header.running_head: Their Voices reaching Far Distant Places

blocks.text: Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "The thought came to my heart that they (our Muslim army) should use the mountain to defend themselves from the enemy. I therefore made the statement hoping that one of Allaah's servants would convey it on my behalf."[^1]

Hadhrat Amr bin Haarith reports that because Hadhrat Umar (RA) was comfortable with Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), it was Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) who approached Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "The worst reprimand I can give the people in your defence is that you give them reason to attack you. You were delivering a lecture when you suddenly shouted, 'The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!' What was this all about?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) explained, "I swear by Allaah that I could not help it. I saw our army fighting near a mountain as they were being attacked from the front and from the back. I could not help shouting 'The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!' so that they retreat towards the mountain."
All the people needed to do was to await a letter from Hadhrat Saariyah (RA), which read, "We met the enemy on a Friday and continued fighting from the time we performed the Fajr salaah until the time for the Jumu'ah salaah arrived and the sun was starting to decline. It was then that we twice heard someone calling, 'The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!' We then retreated towards the mountain and continued gaining the upper hand until Allaah finally defeated them." Thereafter, the people who had been criticising Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "Leave that man (Hadhrat Umar (RA)) alone because he has things made (he has good reason for all that he does)."[^2]
Another narration states that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was asked why he made the statement, he replied, "By Allaah! I said only what was placed on my tongue (by Allaah)."[^3]
The Voice of Hadhrat Abu Qirsaafah (RA) Reaches Far Off

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Izzah bint Aas bin Abu Qirsaafah
blocks.text: Hadhrat Izzah bint Aas bin Abu Qirsaafah reports that the Romans once took one of Hadhrat Abu Qirsaafah (RA)'s sons prisoner. When the time arrived for every salaah, Hadhrat Abu Qirsaafah (RA) used to climb a wall and call out his son's name saying, "Salaah!" His son would then hear his father even though he was in Roman territory.[^4]
